records.text: Hound is a highly aggressive humanoid predator adapted to quadrupedal movement. Appearance: a sickly thin human-like body travels on elongated arms and legs; long black hair obscures much of the head, while sharp claws and an abnormally large mouth packed with sharp teeth become visible at close range. External reference material says eye contact can briefly intimidate one, but Project canon keeps Hounds hostile to humans. They remain fast pursuit predators that pressure injured or isolated prey and can withdraw from strong resistance before returning.

Clump is a compact ambush predator built from a tangled bundle of human-like limbs. Appearance: many arms and legs knot around a dense central mass, with the longest limb able to stretch outward; external descriptions place large recorded specimens around 3 feet across and report a central mouth lined with razor-like teeth. It has extreme speed and agility and favors tight or dark recesses, corners and crawlspaces before seizing prey. Project hard lock: every Clump is hostile to humans; stillness or hiding is never neutrality.

Duller is a fast, deceptively strong humanoid hunter. Appearance: a tall dark-grey, faceless and earless figure with a frail skeletal build, unusually long arms, a wobbly stance and unnatural walking motion; its arms can extend far beyond normal human reach. External reports describe a tactic of remaining in a parallel hall and no-clipping an arm through a wall to seize prey, while a direct approach may make it retreat. Project canon preserves its blind-corner watching behavior and hard-locks every Duller as hostile; retreat is not friendliness.

Deathmoth is an insectoid roaming predator derived from the Backrooms' giant-moth concept. Appearance: the common form has two pairs of membranous scaled wings, compound eyes plus small ocelli, feathered antennae and segmented claw-tipped legs; females are bulkier than males and retain stronger mandibles. Current external lore contains multiple castes and even docile/tamable males, but Project canon rejects any friendly or domesticated interpretation: every encountered Deathmoth is hostile to humans. Combat behavior should preserve aerial harassment, swarming pressure and close-range biting/tearing without importing unlisted caste powers automatically.

Hostile Faceling is a humanoid predator that closely resembles a person except for its missing normal facial features. Appearance: body shape, skin tone, hair, clothing, age and build can vary like humans, but the face remains blank or featureless, creating an otherwise human silhouette at a distance. Current Backrooms Wiki material describes many Facelings as docile and capable of human-like routines and social behavior; Project canon explicitly overrides that disposition. Here, every encountered Faceling is hostile and may imitate ordinary human routines only to lower vigilance, approach and hunt.

False Puddle is an immobile ambush predator disguised as a shallow puddle of Almond Water. Appearance: while dormant it looks like an ordinary flat pool, but beneath the surface is a deep mouth-like pit lined with sharp teeth; when triggered, the apparent puddle becomes the opening of that toothed cavity. External references consistently describe the disguise and trap mechanism, while exact depth and weaknesses vary by source. Project canon keeps the established rule that it reacts to nearby human movement, opens when stepped on, and remains hostile; Liquid Pain or sharp metal are recorded countermeasures, not guaranteed kills.

Paintings are hostile anomalous pictures or drawings that can behave as living predators. Appearance: at rest they can look like ordinary framed canvases or rough drawings; some depict human or other living figures, sometimes with eyes that appear to track nearby people. When prey approaches, a depicted hand, arm, or other limb may extend beyond the image plane to seize and pull the victim into the picture. External references for this Entity are lower-authority Fandom/game material rather than current Wikidot canon. Project canon keeps ENT-1G authoritative: suspicious living Paintings are hostile visual-lure/grab threats and should not be approached or touched without control of the area.

Smiler is a darkness-adapted hostile predator recognized mainly by a face-like pattern glowing in blacked-out areas. Appearance: reflective luminous eyes and a wide row of bright teeth hang in the darkness while the rest of the body is usually obscured or not reliably visible. Current Backrooms Wiki material says Smilers are attracted to light and may react to panic, retreat, loud noise, or loss of eye contact. Project canon keeps ENT-2C authoritative: a Smiler may remain at distance in dark corners to pressure humans toward a bad route instead of immediately charging; every encountered Smiler remains hostile.

Skin-Stealer is a hostile humanoid infiltrator that can disguise itself with human skin. Appearance: its true form is a tall pale-yellow humanoid with sunken white eyes and flesh covered in microscopic sucker-like bumps; when wearing stolen skin it can appear warm and convincingly human. Current Backrooms Wiki material also describes translucent blood and speech mimicry, but portrays unfed individuals as sometimes docile. Project canon overrides that disposition and goes further on infiltration: ENT-2D allows deep behavioral mimicry and enough copied memory to pass simple tests, including long-term group sabotage. Human appearance never proves a contact is human.

Predatory Window is a hostile anomalous window manifestation. Appearance: it can take many ordinary window shapes and styles suited to its surroundings, yet show a blurred, familiar-looking landscape unrelated to the real space beyond the wall; occupied instances contain a dark, indistinct humanoid silhouette with few reliable features. Current Backrooms Wiki material describes lure-like perceived whispers and gestures plus dangerous close interaction. Project canon keeps ENT-2E / ENT-5B authoritative and simpler: impossible placement, deceptive scene or silhouette, unreliable reach, and a grab/pull attack; every instance is hostile.

Biological Pipeline is a vast hostile organic/mechanical pipe-like predator whose visible passage may be only part of its body. Appearance: it presents as a long pipe or crawl-tunnel with flesh-like biological surfaces integrated into otherwise mechanical piping, creating a route that can be mistaken for traversable infrastructure. Lower-authority external material independently describes long flesh-made pipes that digest people who enter, but no current Wikidot Entity article was found for this exact name. Project canon ENT-2F remains authoritative: it can sense prey, lure humans deeper, redirect or lock passage and release tissue-corrosive alkaline liquid; destroying one section does not prove the whole Entity dead.

Wretch is a hostile human-derived creature associated with the Wretched Cycle. Appearance: advanced Wretches are skeletal humanoids with dry reddish-brown flaky skin, holes and pustules, severe tissue loss, displaced or excessive teeth and nails, permanently exposed or distorted eyes, and brown sludge leaking from the mouth or other openings; mutations can add misplaced eyes or deformed limbs. Current Backrooms Wiki says transformation follows deprivation and can produce anything from shambling to very fast, unusually strong individuals. Project canon preserves the established hunting-through-sound-and-scent behavior and does not treat any retained human trace as friendliness or reversibility after a fully hostile encounter.

Hotel Corpse Lure is a Project-original phenomenon/entity whose classification remains OPEN: it may be a separate Entity or a hunting mechanism of the Beast of Level 5. A corpse may stay unnaturally warm, appear to breathe, speak in the victim's own voice, move when unobserved, point toward a door or carry a desirable item. Every apparent sign of life or help is bait; it is hostile to humans and should not be approached or touched until the area is controlled.

Jane the Killer is a roaming humanoid predator. Internet folklore contains multiple incompatible Jane identities and origin stories, so Project canon does not lock a Frontrooms identity, burn history, supernatural power set or relationship to Jeff; survivors use the name only because of resemblance. Jane stalks humans, uses misdirection and close-range ambush, and may use a blade. She is never an ally, trader, rescuer or neutral contact. Whether separate sightings are one individual and what happens after a confirmed kill remain OPEN.

Slenderman is a roaming anomalous humanoid predator. Survivors use the name because the figure resembles the 2009 Internet horror character: unnaturally tall and thin, faceless, dark-suited, sometimes with long appendage-like limbs. Origin and identity are UNKNOWN. Project behavior: it stalks humans across long sightlines, isolates targets and closes for abduction or lethal attack. It is never friendly or neutral. Do not grant teleportation, omniscience or automatic equipment failure; movement and threat positioning must still obey GM fairness, path, time and evidence.

Async Member is a human hostile combatant entry representing an armed Async field member when encountered through the Entity combat roster; this entry does not classify every Async employee as hostile. Base HP pool is 60/60. Base combat stats are HP Stat 7, Defend 8, Agi 9 and Crit 10. Active skill [Let's catch you] rolls once on each Async Member combat turn at 20% proc; when it procs, the attack uses current BaseDMG +20%, resolves through normal Evasion/Critical/DF rules, and on a successful hit applies [Choáng] for 2 turns. Passive [Anysc Evade] is always active and fixes this combatant's Evasion at 25%.

records.text: Gameplay roaming policy: every one of the 19 Entity entries may appear on every playable Level regardless of local environment or resident-population lore. Each entry receives its own independent 3.0000% appearance roll on an eligible physical gameplay turn. Multiple different Entity rolls may succeed in the same turn. This roaming rule does not make an Entity friendly, neutral or resident to a Level.
